claim: β-cytoplasmic actin and γ-cytoplasmic actin are nearly indistinguishable in their amino acid sequence, differing by only four residues within their N-termini.
source: β‐ and γ‐cytoplasmic actin are nearly indistinguishable in their amino acid sequence, but are encoded by different genes that play non‐redundant biological roles.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citation to Vandekerckhove and Weber, 1978 in the introduction.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin are encoded by different genes.
source: β‐ and γ‐cytoplasmic actin are nearly indistinguishable in their amino acid sequence, but are encoded by different genes that play non‐redundant biological roles.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin play non-redundant biological roles.
source: β‐ and γ‐cytoplasmic actin are nearly indistinguishable in their amino acid sequence, but are encoded by different genes that play non‐redundant biological roles.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple citations throughout the manuscript regarding knockout phenotypes.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin mRNA coding sequences differ by nearly 13% due to silent substitutions affecting approximately 40% of their codons.
source: Notably, β-and γ-actin mRNA coding sequences differ much more significantly, by nearly 13%, due to silent substitutions affecting approximately 40% of their codons (Erba et al., 1986).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citation to Erba et al., 1986.

claim: β-actin is translated in bursts and accumulates faster than γ-actin.
source: Recent evidence suggests that this difference in mRNA coding sequence affects translation dynamics of the two actin isoforms: β-actin is translated in bursts and accumulates faster than γ-actin (Buxbaum et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to Buxbaum et al., 2014 and Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: Faster translation of β-actin results in differential post-translational modification by arginylation, which targets only β- but not γ-actin.
source: Such faster translation results in their differential post-translational modification by arginylation, which targets only β- but not γ-actin (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin localize to different parts of the cell and tend to incorporate into different actin cytoskeletal structures.
source: A body of evidence shows that these actins localize to different parts of the cell and tend to incorporate into different actin cytoskeletal structures (Dugina et al., 2009; Kashina, 2006; Otey et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by multiple citations.

claim: β-actin knockout in mice results in early embryonic lethality despite proportional up-regulation of other actin isoforms.
source: More definitively, several studies show that β-actin knockout in mice results in early embryonic lethality despite proportional up-regulation of other actin isoforms to compensate for the total actin dosage (Bunnell et al., 2011; Shawlot et al., 1998; Shmerling et al., 2005; Strathdee et al., 2008; Tondeleir et al., 2013, 2014)
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by multiple citations to knockout studies.

claim: γ-actin knockout in mice has a much milder phenotype that does not interfere with animal survival during embryogenesis.
source: while γ-actin knockout in mice has a much milder phenotype that does not interfere with animal survival during embryogenesis (Belyantseva et al., 2009; Bunnell and Ervasti, 2010).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citations to knockout studies.

claim: The lethality of β-actin knockout in mice can be rescued by a targeted knock-in of the β-actin cDNA.
source: This lethality of β-actin knockout in mice can be rescued by a targeted knock-in of the β-actin cDNA (Tondeleir et al., 2012), suggesting that the coding region of this gene is far more important for organism's survival than any non-coding elements affected by the β-actin knockout.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citation to Tondeleir et al., 2012.

claim: The coding region of the β-actin gene is more important for organism's survival than any non-coding elements affected by the β-actin knockout.
source: This lethality of β-actin knockout in mice can be rescued by a targeted knock-in of the β-actin cDNA (Tondeleir et al., 2012), suggesting that the coding region of this gene is far more important for organism's survival than any non-coding elements affected by the β-actin knockout.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the rescue experiment cited.

claim: Some biochemical differences between β- and γ-actin were observed in polymerization assays both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Some biochemical differences between β- and γ-actin were observed in polymerization assays both in vitro and in vivo (Bergeron et al., 2010; Kapustina et al., 2016; Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: β-actin mRNA, unlike γ-actin mRNA, gets spatially targeted to the cell periphery via zipcode-mediated transport.
source: In addition, β-actin mRNA, unlike γ-actin mRNA, gets spatially targeted to the cell periphery via zipcode-mediated transport (Hill and Gunning, 1993; Kislauskis et al., 1997).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: β- and γ-actin can differentially regulate gene expression of a subset of cytoskeleton proteins.
source: Finally, β- and γ-actin actin can differentially regulate gene expression of a subset of cytoskeleton proteins (Tondeleir et al., 2013, 2014).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: Editing of the β-actin coding sequence to encode γ-actin protein without disruption of the rest of the β-actin gene does not affect mouse survival or produce a visible phenotype at the organismal or cellular level.
source: we demonstrate here that editing of the β-actin coding sequence to encode γ-actin protein without disruption of the rest of the β-actin gene does not affect mouse survival or produce a visible phenotype at the organismal or cellular level.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1-5.

claim: γ-actin protein is functionally capable of substituting for β-actin in the absence of gene disruption.
source: This result shows that γ-actin protein is functionally capable of substituting for β-actin in the absence of gene disruption.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: The differences in in vivo functions of β- and γ-actin are ultimately determined by their nucleotide rather than amino acid sequence.
source: Thus, we demonstrate that the differences in in vivo functions of β- and γ-actin actin are ultimately determined by their nucleotide rather than amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on the experimental data.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing was used to introduce five point mutations into the native mouse β-actin gene (Actb), altering it to encode γ-actin protein.
source: To test whether this essential function of β-actin is defined by its amino acid or nucleotide sequence, we used CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing to introduce five point mutations into the native mouse β-actin gene (Actb), altering it to encode γ-actin protein without changing any of the features of the rest of the gene sequence ('beta-coded gamma actin', Figure 1A).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The edited β-actin gene (Actbc-g) contains the same promoter, as well as the same coding and non-coding elements as the native gene, but produces γ-actin protein.
source: We termed this edited gene Actbc-g, in which the native β-actin gene is nearly intact (with five point mutations within the first 10 codons) and contains the same promoter, as well as the same coding and non-coding elements, but the protein produced from this gene is identical to γ-actin.
evidence: This is directly stated in the description of the experimental design.

claim: Actbc-g mice appeared completely healthy, viable, and fertile with no signs of deficiencies previously seen in any of the β-actin knockout mouse models.
source: Strikingly, Actbc-g mice appeared completely healthy, viable, and fertile with no signs of deficiencies previously seen in any of the β-actin knockout mouse models.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by observational data from the mice.

claim: Actbc-g mice did not exhibit any visible defects in embryogenesis.
source: These mice did not exhibit any visible defects in embryogenesis (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is stated and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Actbc-g mice appeared healthy and normal at birth and throughout life (observed until approximately 8 months old).
source: and appeared healthy and normal at birth and throughout life (Figure 1C) (observed until approximately 8 months old by the time of the submission of this study for publication).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Actbc-g mice had normal fertility, with litter sizes from homozygous breeding pairs averaging 6.4 pups per litter (±0.38 SEM, n = 9).
source: These mice also had normal fertility, as evidenced by litter sizes from Actbc-g homozygous breeding pairs that averaged 6.4 pups per litter (±0.38 SEM, n = 9), compared to the average litter size of 6.3 pups previously reported for their matching background wild type strain C57BL/6 (http://www.informatics.jax.org/silver/tables/table4-1.shtml).
evidence: This is directly stated with quantitative data.

claim: The average litter size for wild type C57BL/6 mice is 6.3 pups.
source: compared to the average litter size of 6.3 pups previously reported for their matching background wild type strain C57BL/6 (http://www.informatics.jax.org/silver/tables/table4-1.shtml).
evidence: This is stated with a reference to published data.

claim: β-actin nucleotide sequence, rather than its amino acid sequence, determines the essential function of β-actin in vivo.
source: Thus, this result definitively proves that β-actin nucleotide sequence, rather than its amino acid sequence, determines the essential function of β-actin in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: No overall differences or abnormalities were found between wild type and Actbc-g mice in the morphology and appearance of all major organs and body parts in newborn (P0) mice.
source: To test for possible milder defects in these mice, we analyzed the overall morphology and appearance of all major organs and body parts in newborn (P0) Actbc-g mice by sagittal sectioning and H&E staining, and found no overall differences or abnormalities between wild type and Actbc-g mice (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Embryonic development in Actbc-g mice occurs normally.
source: suggesting that the embryonic development in these mice occurs normally.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the histological analysis.

claim: In Actbc-g mice, loss of β-actin protein was accompanied by a prominent increase in γ-actin, without overall changes in total actin levels in brain, kidney, liver, and lungs.
source: In all these tissues, loss of β-actin protein was accompanied by a prominent increase in γ-actin, without overall changes in total actin levels (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 2 and supplementary figures.

claim: Corresponding changes in actin isoforms were seen on 2D gels from brain, kidney, liver, and lung tissues, run under shallow pH gradient to separate actin isoforms.
source: Corresponding changes were also seen on 2D gels from these tissues, run under shallow pH gradient to separate actin isoforms (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing was used to edit the mouse γ-actin gene to encode β-actin protein.
source: We also performed a reciprocal experiment, using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to edit the mouse γ-actin gene to encode β-actin protein ('gamma-coded beta actin' or γc-β-actin, Figure 2—figure supplements 3–4).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The γ-actin gene editing strategy was only partially successful, resulting in replacement of the first three nucleotides to convert the N-terminal MEEE sequence of γ-actin into the MDDD sequence of β-actin, while failing to achieve I/V substitution at codon 10.
source: This strategy was only partially successful, resulting in replacement of the first three nucleotides to convert the N-terminal MEEE sequence of γ-actin into the MDDD sequence of β-actin, while failing to achieve I/V substitution at codon 10.
evidence: This is directly stated in the description of the experimental results.

claim: Actg1c-b mice showed no detectable phenotype.
source: These Actg1c-b mice showed no detectable phenotype.
evidence: This is directly stated based on observational data.

claim: Actg1c-b mice showed disappearance of γ-actin protein and a corresponding increase in β-actin-like protein by western blots.
source: At the same time, they showed disappearance of γ-actin protein and a corresponding increase in β-actin-like protein by western blots (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in supplementary figure.

claim: γ-actin in vivo functions, like β-actin, is also defined by its nucleotide, rather than amino acid sequence.
source: These results suggest that γ-actin in vivo functions, like β-actin, is also defined by its nucleotide, rather than amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the Actg1c-b mouse data.

claim: β-actin has been previously shown to play a major role in directional cell migration.
source: Since β-actin has been previously shown to play a major role in directional cell migration, and its knockout in cells leads to severe impairments in their actin cytoskeleton organization and their ability to migrate (Bunnell et al., 2011; Tondeleir et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: β-actin knockout in cells leads to severe impairments in their actin cytoskeleton organization and their ability to migrate.
source: Since β-actin has been previously shown to play a major role in directional cell migration, and its knockout in cells leads to severe impairments in their actin cytoskeleton organization and their ability to migrate (Bunnell et al., 2011; Tondeleir et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: No difference in F-actin levels was detected between wild type and Actbc-g mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: We detected no difference in F-actin levels in these cells (Figure 3)
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 3.

claim: No difference in the morphology and appearance of the actin cytoskeleton was observed between wild type and Actbc-g mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: or in the morphology and appearance of the actin cytoskeleton (Figure 3 and Figure 4).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: No difference was observed in overall migration rates of cell monolayers between wild type and Actbc-g mouse embryonic fibroblasts in wound healing assays.
source: To test the ability of these cells to migrate, we performed wound healing assays to measure the overall migration rates of the cell monolayers in wild type and Actbc-g. We also measured the directionality of single cell migration on fibronectin-coated dishes. In both assays, no difference was observed between the two cell types (Figure 5 and Figure 5—videos 1 and 2)
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 5.

claim: No difference was observed in the directionality of single cell migration on fibronectin-coated dishes between wild type and Actbc-g mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: To test the ability of these cells to migrate, we performed wound healing assays to measure the overall migration rates of the cell monolayers in wild type and Actbc-g. We also measured the directionality of single cell migration on fibronectin-coated dishes. In both assays, no difference was observed between the two cell types (Figure 5 and Figure 5—videos 1 and 2)
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The actin isoform substitution did not result in any significant changes in the cells' ability to migrate.
source: confirming that the actin isoform substitution did not result in any significant changes in these cells' ability to migrate.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the migration assay data.

claim: The ribosome density on mouse β-actin mRNA is over a thousand fold higher than γ-actin (average ribosome density over the first 150 codons: 1351.607 for β-actin versus 1.289 for γ-actin).
source: Remarkably, composite data from 26 independently performed ribosome profiling studies from different mouse tissues show that the ribosome density on mouse β-actin mRNA is over a thousand fold higher than γ-actin (average ribosome density over the first 150 codons: 1351.607 for β-actin versus 1.289 for γ-actin, see also Table 1 and Supplementary file 1 and 2)
evidence: This is directly stated with quantitative data from ribosome profiling analysis.

claim: The translation dynamics of β-actin in vivo is dramatically different from that of γ-actin.
source: These data suggest that the translation dynamics of β-actin in vivo is dramatically different from that of γ-actin.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the ribosome density data.

claim: Members of the actin family have vastly different ribosome densities, with β-actin being by far the highest, while γ-enteric smooth muscle actin is by far the lowest (ribosome density 0.377).
source: This analysis shows that members of the actin family have vastly different ribosome densities, with β-actin being by far the highest, while γ-enteric smooth muscle actin is by far the lowest (ribosome density 0.377)
evidence: This is directly stated based on analysis of ribosome profiling data shown in Table 1.

claim: The intracellular accumulation rate and translation dynamics for β-actin and γ-enteric smooth muscle actin should be vastly different from each other.
source: suggesting that the intracellular accumulation rate for these two proteins, as well as their translation dynamics, should be vastly different from each other.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the ribosome density differences.

claim: β-actin and γ-enteric smooth muscle actin have different mRNA structures in the coding region.
source: In support, they also have different mRNA structures in the coding region (Zhang et al., 2010, Supplementary file 3 and 4).
evidence: This is stated with citation and reference to supplementary data.

claim: The actin isoforms that tend to become up-regulated in different knockout models are typically those with the closest ribosome density to the isoform that had been knocked out.
source: Notably, the actin isoforms that tend to become up-regulated in different knockout models are typically those with the closest ribosome density to the isoform that had been knocked out (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data in Table 1.

claim: Alpha skeletal and alpha smooth muscle actins appear to partially cross-compensate for each other, and these isoforms are the second and third highest by ribosome density, after β-actin.
source: For instance, alpha skeletal and alpha smooth muscle actins appear to partially cross-compensate for each other, and these isoforms are also the second and third highest by ribosome density, after β-actin.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of knockout data and ribosome density.

claim: α-cardiac actin completely rescues knockout of α-skeletal actin, which has the closest ribosome density.
source: α-cardiac actin completely rescues knockout of α-skeletal actin, which has the closest ribosome density.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of knockout data and ribosome density.

claim: Loss of α-cardiac actin cannot be substituted for by γ-enteric smooth muscle actin, which has a ~10 fold lower ribosome density.
source: In contrast, loss of α-cardiac actin cannot be substituted for by γ-enteric smooth muscle actin, which has a ~10 fold lower ribosome density.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of knockout data and ribosome density.

claim: Actin isoforms with similar ribosome density can plausibly compensate for the loss of one of the isoforms.
source: These results suggest the actin isoform with similar ribosome density can plausibly compensate for the loss of one of the isoforms.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analysis of knockout and ribosome density data.

claim: Given the orders of magnitude difference in ribosome density between β-actin and other actin isoforms, none of the other actin isoforms can compensate for the loss of β-actin.
source: In agreement, given the orders of magnitude difference in ribosome density between β-actin and other actin isoforms, none of the other actin isoforms can compensate for the loss of β-actin.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the ribosome density analysis.

claim: Changes in ribosome density arising from silent substitutions in nucleotide sequence affect translation dynamics and protein accumulation rates, which in turn regulate functional diversity of actins.
source: We propose that changes in ribosome density arising from silent substitutions in nucleotide sequence, affect translation dynamics and protein accumulation rates, which in turn regulate functional diversity of actins.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed mechanism based on the data.

claim: A search of the mouse genome for proteins that are over 90% identical both in length and in their amino acid sequence over their entire length, and are encoded by different genes, yielded 741 families encoding nearly 4000 different open reading frames.
source: First, to identify all protein families encoding highly similar proteins, we searched the mouse genome for proteins that are over 90% identical both in length and in their amino acid sequence over their entire length, and are encoded by different genes. This search yielded 741 families in mouse, encoding nearly 4000 different open reading frames.
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of the bioinformatic analysis.

claim: The top families with high standard deviation of ribosome densities identified in mouse, human, and zebrafish genomes were similar and included the actin family as one of the top hits.
source: The top families identified in these searches were similar in all three vertebrate genomes, and contained the actin family as one of the top hits.
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of the comparative genomic analysis.

claim: The other uniformly present top hits in mouse, human, and zebrafish included multiple classes of histones and tubulins.
source: The other uniformly present top hits included multiple classes of histones and tubulins.
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of the comparative genomic analysis.

claim: Analysis of D. melanogaster and C. elegans genomes also yielded actins, tubulins, and histones as the top hits.
source: Notably, similar analysis of D. melanogaster and C. elegans genomes (Supplementary files 4 and 5) also yielded actins, tubulins, and histones as the top hits.
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of the comparative genomic analysis.

claim: The occurrence of families of nearly identical proteins with vastly different ribosome densities may be broadly common in higher eukaryotes.
source: Thus, the occurrence of families of nearly identical proteins with vastly different ribosome densities may be broadly common in higher eukaryotes, supporting our idea that this feature may underlie their functional regulation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the comparative genomic analysis.

claim: Posttranscriptional regulation of highly homologous proteins in seemingly redundant protein families through silent nucleotide-encoded translation dynamics constitutes a novel type of functional regulation that governs some of the most essential functions in eukaryotic genomes.
source: We propose that posttranscriptional regulation of highly homologous proteins in seemingly redundant protein families through silent nucleotide-encoded translation dynamics constitutes a novel type of functional regulation that governs some of the most essential functions in eukaryotic genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed mechanism based on the data.

claim: The proposed regulation mechanism is termed 'silent code', to reflect its origin in silent substitutions within the genetic code.
source: We propose to term this regulation 'silent code', to reflect its origin in silent substitutions within the genetic code.
evidence: This is directly stated as a proposed terminology.

claim: Silent substitutions in nucleotide sequence are a novel determinant that drives the differential functions of non-muscle actin isoforms.
source: Our results demonstrate a novel determinant – silent substitutions in nucleotide sequence – that drives the differential functions of non-muscle actin isoforms, a mechanism potentially applicable to other members of the actin family and other highly similar proteins in eukaryotic genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: The mechanism of silent substitutions driving differential functions is potentially applicable to other members of the actin family and other highly similar proteins in eukaryotic genomes.
source: Our results demonstrate a novel determinant – silent substitutions in nucleotide sequence – that drives the differential functions of non-muscle actin isoforms, a mechanism potentially applicable to other members of the actin family and other highly similar proteins in eukaryotic genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed extension of the findings.

claim: The nucleotide sequence of the gene, rather than the amino acid sequence of the encoded isoform, determines the absolute requirement of β-actin for organism's survival.
source: Our data demonstrate that the nucleotide sequence of the gene, rather than the amino acid sequence of the encoded isoform, determines the absolute requirement of β-actin for organism's survival.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin isoforms have slightly different polymerization kinetics.
source: While β-actin and γ-actin isoforms share a remarkable conservation at the amino acid level, with just four homologous amino changes at their N-termini, these two proteins have been shown to have slightly different polymerization kinetics (Bergeron et al., 2010)
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin differentially interact with cofilin.
source: and to differentially interact with cofilin (Kapustina et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: β-actin and γ-actin differentially interact with non-muscle myosin isoforms.
source: and non-muscle myosin isoforms (Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Actin 3′UTRs are isoform-specific and evolutionarily conserved.
source: At the level of mRNA, actin 3′UTRs are isoform-specific and evolutionarily conserved, suggesting that they play important roles in vivo (Erba et al., 1986; Hill and Gunning, 1993).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: β-actin 3′UTR is important for the localization of the transcript.
source: A plethora of literature elucidates the importance of β-actin 3′UTR for the localization of the transcript (see, e.g. (Condeelis and Singer, 2005) for a comprehensive review).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a review.

claim: γ-actin mRNA induces a ribosome pausing event, resulting in its slower translation compared to β-actin, a mechanism that drives their differential arginylation.
source: It has also been shown that γ-actin mRNA induces a ribosome pausing event, resulting in its slower translation compared to β-actin, a mechanism that drives their differential arginylation (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: An alternative poly A site in β-actin mRNA increases its translation levels.
source: An alternative poly A site in β-actin mRNA increases its translation levels (Ghosh et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: γ-actin gene contains a unique and highly conserved intron III.
source: γ-actin gene contains a unique and highly conserved intron III (Lloyd and Gunning, 1993)
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: γ-actin gene contains an alternatively spliced exon 3a.
source: and an alternatively spliced exon 3a (Drummond and Friderici, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: β-actin exhibits both 3′UTR-dependent and 3′UTR-independent feedback regulation of gene expression.
source: β-actin exhibits both 3′UTR-dependent (Lloyd and Gunning, 1993; Lyubimova et al., 1999) and 3′UTR-independent (Lloyd et al., 1992; Schevzov et al., 1992) feedback regulation of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Among the 6 members of the actin family in mice, β-actin by far has the highest representation in the polysome fraction.
source: Ribosome profiling experiments show that among the 6 members of the actin family in mice, β-actin by far has the highest representation in the polysome fraction (Ingolia et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation to ribosome profiling data.

claim: High ribosome density confers the cell with the ability to spatially and temporally fine tune translation of β-actin and the local and global rate of its intracellular accumulation.
source: We propose that this confers the cell with the ability to spatially and temporally fine tune translation of β-actin and the local and global rate of its intracellular accumulation (Buxbaum et al., 2014; Ströhl et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated as a proposed mechanism with supporting citations.

claim: High ribosome density makes β-actin the most essential of the actin isoforms and cannot be compensated for when deleted.
source: and thus makes β-actin the most essential of the actin isoforms and cannot be compensated for when deleted.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the ribosome density analysis.

claim: Non-muscle γ-actin appears to be more functionally redundant and can be largely compensated for by other actins that have similar ribosome densities.
source: The nearly identical non-muscle γ-actin appears to be more functionally redundant and can be largely compensated for by other actins that have similar ribosome densities (Perrin and Ervasti, 2010), Table 1, and Supplementary file 2 and 3).
evidence: This is stated with citation and reference to data tables.

claim: Actin isoforms with similar ribosome densities and translation dynamics are more likely to compensate for each other's functions.
source: Our findings suggest that actin isoforms with similar ribosome densities and translation dynamics are more likely to compensate for each other's functions
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: β-actin, with the highest-ribosome-density is unique in its functional significance.
source: while β-actin, with the highest-ribosome-density is unique in its functional significance.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Deletion of exons 2 and 3 of the β-actin gene that include β-actin translation initiation site but do not encompass the promoter region, UTR, or the non-coding elements in the rest of the gene leads to embryonic lethality.
source: Indeed, deletion of exons 2 and 3 of the β-actin gene that include β-actin translation initiation site but do not encompass the promoter region, UTR, or the non-coding elements in the rest of the gene leads to embryonic lethality (Bunnell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: In Actb knockout mice other actin isoforms are up-regulated to compensate for the total actin dosage, but this promoter-mediated up-regulation is insufficient to rescue the phenotype of early embryonic lethality.
source: Notably, in Actb knockout mice other actin isoforms are up-regulated to compensate for the total actin dosage, but this promoter-mediated up-regulation is insufficient to rescue the phenotype of early embryonic lethality.
evidence: This is stated based on previous knockout studies.

claim: Targeted insertion of the human β-actin coding sequence into the β-actin gene region rescues embryonic lethality in β-actin knockout mice.
source: At the same time, targeted insertion of the human β-actin coding sequence into this region rescues embryonic lethality in these mice, further supporting the idea that the coding sequence plays a key role (Tondeleir et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Coding sequence drives differences in actin's posttranslational modifications, one of the forms of functional actin regulation.
source: Data from our group previously showed that coding sequence drives differences in actin's posttranslational modifications, one of the forms of functional actin regulation (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work from the authors' group.

claim: The coding region is primarily responsible for the uniquely essential role of β-actin in vivo.
source: While these studies do not fully exclude a potential contribution of non-coding elements, especially those that may be located between exons 2 and 3 in the gene, they strongly support our hypothesis that the coding region is primarily responsible for the uniquely essential role of β-actin in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the cited studies.

claim: Non-muscle actin isoform genes have evolutionarily diverged >100 million years ago.
source: Despite the fact that non-muscle actin isoform genes have evolutionarily diverged >100 million years ago
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Non-muscle actin isoform genes have retained remarkable sequence conservation, far higher than what would be expected if the synonymous substitutions in their coding sequence were completely randomized.
source: they have retained remarkable sequence conservation, far higher than what would be expected if the synonymous substitutions in their coding sequence were completely randomized (Erba et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Actin isoform coding sequence exists under additional evolutionary pressure, over and above the conservation of amino acid sequence.
source: This is consistent with our idea that actin isoform coding sequence exists under additional evolutionary pressure, over and above the conservation of amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the conservation data.

claim: At least some of the evolutionary pressure on actin isoform coding sequence is aimed to maintain the divergent translation dynamics within the actin family, in order to drive their divergent functions.
source: We propose that at least some of this pressure is aimed to maintain the divergent translation dynamics within the actin family, in order to drive their divergent functions.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed mechanism.

claim: Tubulin is one of the top candidate families for regulation through 'silent code' in addition to actin.
source: Notably, one of the top candidate families for this regulation in addition to actin – tubulin – is also a major cytoskeletal protein regulated by multiple posttranslational modifications.
evidence: This is stated based on the bioinformatic analysis.

claim: Some members of the tubulin family conceivably may be regulated via silent substitutions in their coding sequence affecting translation dynamics, like shown previously for non-muscle actins.
source: Some members of the tubulin family conceivably may be regulated via silent substitutions in their coding sequence affecting translation dynamics, like shown previously for non-muscle actins.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on analogy with actins.

claim: Tubulin β-V (Tubb5) is likely the most essential of the β-tubulin genes, whose knockout likely cannot be substituted by up-regulation of any other β-tubulin.
